title: [Lean] Execute padded signed addition with linear resource bounds
body:
## Executed finite-word result

Explicit author-checked context: upstream main 0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea; kappa = 836330098538459/500000000000000000 = 0.001672660197076918. These generic machines do not change or establish the selected multiplication exponent.

Six independently checked modules implement signed alignment, a marked ripple adder, paid sign-extension/pair layout, layout-to-adder switching, and the complete seven-tape padding-to-sum controller with its derived resource invoice. They execute both padding runs and three charged controller switches. Original source/control tapes are retained, output workspaces start blank, and heads return to their specified markers.

For LA=dx+length(xs), LB=dy+length(ys), M=max(LA,LB), the actual first halt is 19M+7(LA+LB)+89 transitions. Every prefix uses at most 2(LA+LB)+M+16 represented cells. With actual entrance volume V=LA+LB+8, this gives time at most 26V and cells at most 3V. Finite control, sign bits and fixed Boolean registers add constant storage. Cells are finite-alphabet tape cells, not a newly proved bit encoding.

Finite coverage: arbitrary finite low-bit-first Boolean input words, separately supplied signs and nonnegative shifts, including empty words and zero shifts.
Conditional-interface coverage: the caller supplies marked words, unary shift controls and blank disjoint workspace. The output represents 2^dx*signedValue(xs,sx)+2^dy*signedValue(ys,sy). No endpoint equation or uniform running-time majorant is assumed.
Full-theorem coverage: selected encoding, binary exponent differences/control generation, arbitrary dirty-state restoration, physical address allocation, other multiplier events, recursive payload partition and the all-size multiplication/runtime theorem remain open. The coefficient 26 belongs to this prepared routine, not the selected program's uniform C.

## Reproduction and evidence

The six new sources contain 41 standard-only axiom probes and ten full printed types, independently accepted without diagnostics. Public-safe ACCEPTANCE.json binds source identities, scopes and reviewer roles. Detailed original evidence remains preserved with the authors. Reproduction commands pin Lean 4.21.0 and Mathlib 308445d7985027f538e281e18df29ca16ede2ba3. Commands are provided, not claimed as a fresh relocated replay; no extra local CI preflight was run for submission.

Reuse four unchanged public modules without copying them: PR1840 at 3f1b0641d5866f9d0b6cdd8e46db416fed6c5645 and PR1869 at 65ab016b4a464e3f5e2dd26c1bb0ae477e1ebce8. The latter public arithmetic prerequisite retains its documented harmless style warning.

## Scoped overlap and attribution

The bounded comparison inspected PR64 (2d970ab3ca0271cfb2b609dc9aae1b7073b7774d), PR488 (34eb901441affffaba76b00920f2f9cb05777117), PR511 (1ece74dc70a421cfd4e23e8b59ab9e3645872950), PR519 (080c0a17307919a568cf5b919101c9b6f5c42bcd), PR565 (890b2906ebb76b3c9392a08d64e933630c06b1ac), and the public prerequisites. Their counting, allocation, compact-copy and unsigned work-copy interfaces do not supply this paid signed-layout and seven-tape composition. No first-ever arithmetic/tape or optimality claim is made.

James Chang with OpenAI assistance, Apache-2.0. Existing source notices, public prerequisite credit and Lean/Mathlib attribution are retained. Follow-on binary-control production is deliberately separate from this frozen completed chunk.
